description: §6.7.1a — the reactive-assign form `@status = risky() !{ | ::Boom :> "caught" }` inside an `on mount { }` body. Pre-fix this form COMPILED but SILENTLY DROPPED the `!{}` arm (the string rewriter emitted `_scrml_reactive_set("status", risky())`, discarding the handler) — a silent error-handling loss, worse than the loud E-CODEGEN failure of the `let` form. The fix routes the mount body through the real statement codegen, so the recovery arm executes and "caught" (not the raw {__scrml_error} envelope) lands in @status. No input — the boot/mount shape.
rationale: §6.7.1a sugar-equivalence — the `@cell = call() !{...}` recovery-into-cell contract (§19.4.3) must hold inside `on mount` exactly as inside a `function`. risky() fails Boom; the ::Boom recovery arm produces "caught", which is the value written to @status. A dropped arm would leave the raw error envelope (or the un-recovered call) in the cell — the regression this pins against.
